samples.summary: Canonical CLI design doc still states the HTTP client is "built-in `fetch` (Node.js 18+)" while this change makes `undici` a direct runtime dependency and raises `engines.node` to `>=20.18.1`
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:87 (§1 Technology and Distribution) is unchanged: "- **HTTP client**: built-in `fetch` (Node.js 18+)." The diff adds `undici: ^7.29.0` to packages/cli/package.json dependencies, changes `engines.node` from `>=20` to `>=20.18.1`, and image-fetcher.ts now imports `fetch`/`request`/`Agent`/`ProxyAgent` from undici. The new §8.1 prose does mention "the CLI depends on `undici` directly", but the tech-stack section that a reader consults for the runtime contract now contradicts the code and the published package's engine range. Design-doc discipline expects the canonical subsystem doc to be updated for an architecture/dependency change, not only in a subsection.

samples.summary: Raising the published CLI's minimum Node from >=20 to >=20.18.1 is a user-visible compatibility decision with no recorded rationale in the design doc or task doc
samples.evidence: `engines.node` goes `>=20` → `>=20.18.1` (undici 7's floor). Nothing in docs/design/cli.md, docs/design/rest-api.md, or docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-todo.md records that the exit-code work narrows the supported runtime for an already-published npm package — the same kind of published-client compatibility argument the diff makes very carefully for the nonce guard is not made here.

samples.summary: Substantial scope beyond the originating issue (#586 CLI exit codes): a full SSRF gate, IPv6/NAT64/6to4/Teredo address classifier, DNS-rebinding pin, and egress-proxy environment support
samples.evidence: The originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260803-cli-system-exit-code-todo.md) scopes 7 items, all about classifying failures into exit codes 1/2; its Non-goals list error-body shape and retries. This diff additionally lands ~500 lines of network-security machinery in image-fetcher.ts plus the nonce-bound login flow across backend and CLI. The lessons doc records that review deliberately re-accepted this creep ("a control removed from a diff that ships the code it was protecting is not deferred, it is deleted"), so this is noted rather than an objection to the controls themselves — but it makes a single PR carry three independently reviewable subsystems and correspondingly wide blast radius.

samples.summary: Hand-rolled `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`all_proxy`/`no_proxy` parsing reimplements functionality undici (now a direct dependency) already ships as `EnvHttpProxyAgent`
samples.evidence: `proxyForUrl`, `envValue`, `splitHostPort` and `bypassesProxy` (~60 lines plus a test block) re-derive the conventional proxy env semantics, while the same PR adds `undici@^7` as a dependency — undici ≥6.19 exposes `EnvHttpProxyAgent`, which implements exactly this selection including `no_proxy`. The pin/proxy interaction may still need a boolean "does a proxy apply" query, but that is a much smaller surface than a private reimplementation of the parsing rules. Repo convention is reuse over reinvention.

samples.summary: A general network-security module (scheme allowlist, private-address classifier, DNS pin, proxy selection, redirect loop) lives under `src/docs/`, though slides export consumes it too
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:13 imports `createImageFetcher` from `../docs/image-fetcher.js`, and pptx export uses it at slides.ts:214. The cross-area import predates this change, but the file has grown from a ~50-line URL resolver into the CLI's whole outbound-request policy; a `src/net/` (or similar) home would match the layering the rest of the CLI uses (`src/errors.ts`, `src/output/`, `src/client/`) and stop slides depending on a docs-namespaced module for its egress policy.

samples.summary: Unrelated edits to the changed-areas test harness (GIT_* env scrubbing) plus two whitespace-only lines ride along in a CLI exit-code PR
samples.evidence: scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs gains a module-scope loop deleting every `GIT_*` env var — a fix for a pre-push/hook interaction that has nothing to do with issue #586 — and the diff also inserts blank, whitespace-only lines at 410 and 599 inside `execFileSync` option objects (confirmed present in the working tree). The env fix may well be correct, but it belongs to its own change; the whitespace is pure noise (nothing in CI checks formatting, so no lane will catch it).
